semantics.clock: rising edge of clk (conventional D flip-flop interpretation)
semantics.update: At each rising edge, q becomes 0 if r is high, otherwise q becomes sampled d.
semantics.reset: Active-high synchronous reset; r takes priority over d. Reset transitions alone do not change q.
semantics.hold: q holds between rising clock edges, including falling edges.
semantics.initialization: No specified power-up value; no RTL initialization. Tests establish known state with a clocked reset.
semantics.latency: Sampled input appears at q after the same rising edge register update; one sample per rising edge.

verification.oracle: Independent edge-based expected value: r ? 0 : d, checked after nonblocking assignments settle.
verification.directed: Cover all four binary r/d combinations, repeated samples, reset with d high, and reset release.
verification.timing: Toggle d and assert/deassert r between edges and check q holds; check falling edges hold.
verification.initialization: Do not assert a value before the first clocked reset.
verification.tools: Icarus v12, -g2012, explicit dev_tb top; finite compile and simulation timeouts.

specification_ambiguities: Clock edge is not explicitly stated; use the conventional rising edge for a simple D flip-flop.
Power-up output is unspecified; no initial value is imposed.
